pdf.disclaimer.text: Notice: PulseWise AI reports are generated for educational and research purposes only. 'Model-Estimated Risk Score' is a statistical model output trained on CDC BRFSS survey data. Consult a qualified physician for any health decisions.
rec.highbp: High blood pressure is a key cardiovascular factor. General wellness practices like sodium reduction, regular walking, and stress management are widely recommended. Consult a healthcare provider.
rec.highchol: High cholesterol is a known risk factor. Reducing saturated fats and increasing soluble fiber support healthy cholesterol levels. Consult your doctor.
rec.bmi.overweight: BMI above 25 is associated with elevated health risks. Balanced nutrition and regular physical activity are recommended.
rec.bmi.obese: BMI above 30 is linked to higher cardiovascular risk. Consider discussing wellness strategies with a qualified provider.
rec.smoker: Smoking is a primary modifiable risk factor. Public health organizations strongly recommend smoking cessation programs.
rec.physactivity: Low physical activity increases cardiovascular risk. Guidelines suggest at least 150 minutes of moderate activity weekly.
rec.fruits: Eating fresh fruit daily provides essential vitamins and fiber for overall heart health.
rec.veggies: Daily vegetable intake is universally recommended by dietary guidelines for cardiovascular wellness.
rec.hvyalcohol: Heavy alcohol consumption increases health risks. Limiting alcohol intake is advised by health guidelines.
rec.genhlth.fair: Fair general health suggests focusing on regular preventive check-ups and maintaining a consistent healthy routine.
rec.genhlth.poor: Poor general health warrants regular consultation with a qualified medical professional.
rec.menthlth: Several days of poor mental health were reported. Sleep, mindfulness, and social support enhance mental wellness.
rec.diffwalk: Mobility difficulties impact overall activity. Low-impact exercises like swimming or water aerobics are often beneficial.
rec.healthcare: Access to regular healthcare is fundamental to preventive wellness.
rec.stroke: A history of stroke requires ongoing medical supervision and lifestyle risk factor awareness.
rec.diabetes.pre: Pre-diabetes can often be managed through dietary improvements and physical activity. Consult a provider.
rec.diabetes.yes: Managing blood sugar through diet, exercise, and medical supervision is crucial for diabetes care.
rec.default: Based on your inputs, no specific elevated risk factors were flagged. Continue maintaining a balanced lifestyle.

coach.title: 🤖 AI Wellness Coach
coach.subtitle: Personalized general wellness guidance for a healthier heart and lifestyle.
coach.subtitle_user: Hello, {username}! Here are your personalized wellness tips for a healthier heart.
coach.activity.title: Daily Activity
coach.activity.tip1: Start your morning with a 10-minute brisk walk to boost circulation and energy.
coach.activity.tip2: Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity per week (e.g., walking, cycling).
coach.activity.tip3: Take short 5-minute movement breaks every hour if you have a desk job.
coach.activity.tip4: Evening stretching or light yoga helps relax muscles and improves sleep quality.
coach.nutrition.title: Nutrition
coach.nutrition.tip1: Eat at least 2 servings of fruit and 3 servings of vegetables daily.
coach.nutrition.tip2: Choose whole grains, legumes, and healthy fats (nuts, olive oil) over processed foods.
coach.nutrition.tip3: Reduce sodium intake — avoid added salt and processed/packaged snacks.
coach.nutrition.tip4: Stay hydrated: drink 8–10 glasses of water throughout the day.
coach.sleep.title: Sleep
coach.sleep.tip1: Aim for 7–8 hours of restful sleep every night to support heart health.
coach.sleep.tip2: Maintain a consistent sleep schedule — go to bed and wake up at the same time daily.
coach.sleep.tip3: Avoid screens (phone, TV) at least 45 minutes before bedtime to improve sleep quality.
coach.stress.title: Stress Management
coach.stress.tip1: Practice 10–15 minutes of deep breathing or guided mindfulness each day.
coach.stress.tip2: Take three short 2-minute breathing breaks during stressful work hours.
coach.stress.tip3: Connect with friends and family regularly — social support reduces stress hormones.
coach.monitoring.title: Health Monitoring
coach.monitoring.tip1: Schedule regular check-ups with your doctor at least once a year.
coach.monitoring.tip2: Monitor your blood pressure at home if recommended by your healthcare provider.
coach.monitoring.tip3: Get your cholesterol and blood sugar checked as part of routine health screening.
coach.monitoring.tip4: Keep a log of your symptoms, medications, and health metrics to share with your doctor.

insights.title: Model Insights
insights.subtitle: Complete evaluation results, SHAP explainability, and model selection rationale for the Heart Health Hub pipeline.
insights.step1_desc: Your age, vitals, lifestyle and medical history are entered through a structured assessment form.
insights.step2_title: The ML model analyzes your inputs
insights.step2_desc: A Logistic Regression model trained on 253,680 CDC BRFSS survey records processes your 21 health indicators.
insights.step3_desc: The model outputs a statistical probability estimate — not a clinical diagnosis or medical test result.
insights.step4_desc: SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) mathematically identifies which inputs influenced the score and in what direction.
insights.step5_desc: You can modify hypothetical inputs and re-run the existing model to see how the estimated score changes statistically.
insights.step6_desc: The wellness coach offers general wellness information based on your context — it is not a healthcare provider.
insights.step7_desc: The model has limitations and may not generalize to every individual. Always consult a qualified healthcare professional.
insights.why_lr_desc: After evaluating six models on the CDC BRFSS 2015 dataset (253,680 records), Logistic Regression was selected as the production model for the following reasons:
insights.lr_reason1_desc: Minimizes missed positive cases — critical for health screening
insights.lr_reason3_desc: Supports LinearExplainer for fast, exact SHAP values
insights.lr_reason4_desc: Coefficients directly reveal feature influence direction
insights.lr_reason6_desc: Model is fixed and version-controlled for reproducibility
insights.shap_desc1: SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) is a unified mathematical framework for explaining individual model predictions. Each SHAP value quantifies the marginal contribution of a single feature to the model output relative to the expected baseline. Positive values push the score above baseline (toward positive class), while negative values push it below. Heart Health Hub uses the LinearExplainer for fast, exact SHAP values on the Logistic Regression model.
insights.shap_desc2: Global SHAP (above) shows mean absolute SHAP values across all predictions — indicating which features have the most consistent influence. Local SHAP (visible after your prediction) shows how each of your specific inputs shifted the model output above or below the expected baseline.
insights.research_warning: ⚠️ Research & Educational Tool: Heart Health Hub is a research platform. All model outputs are statistical estimates — not medical diagnoses, FDA-cleared tools, or replacements for professional healthcare.
charts.recall_sub: Sensitivity across 6 evaluated algorithms. Higher Recall minimizes missed positive cases.
charts.recall_note: Logistic Regression (78.66% Recall) was selected because in health screening, capturing positives is the priority. Random Forest hit 89.88% accuracy by predicting majority-negative, yet missed 86% of positive cases.
charts.grouped_sub: Side-by-side Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, and ROC-AUC for all six algorithms.
charts.grouped_note: Metrics reveal the class-imbalance trade-off. Logistic Regression and Linear SVM achieve the best balanced performance across Recall (78.66%) and ROC-AUC (84.51%).
charts.dist_sub: 253,680 survey records showing severe class imbalance (9.4% positive rate).
charts.dist_note: SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique) was applied on the training split to handle class imbalance without data leakage.
charts.shap_sub: Mean absolute SHAP value across all 253,680 dataset records.
charts.shap_note: GeneralHealth rating, Age group, High Blood Pressure, and BMI emerge as the top population-wide risk drivers in the trained model.
